Suggested route: (a) far from each other the records are free, so a kept current forces every collision to keep the total two-step momentum sum_i j(k_i) (single-branch wave packets, i[H, G] averaging to zero for local G); at fixed total crystal momentum and energy the collision channels form a curve on which sum_i j varies, so a local (analytic in the channel) scattering amplitude must vanish off the forward and exchange channels: the pair must be transparent; (b) compare with the free pair: the excluded space lacks one on-site state per total momentum (antisymmetric: the singlet with opposite coins), so a counting argument of Levinson's type (the band's phase-shift winding equals the number of states removed or bound) forbids transparency at every energy; (c) make each step exact where possible (finite-torus spectral counts, exact resolvent entries) and name any step that stays assumed. HIT: a proof that no such V exists, or an explicit V that keeps the current, with exact checks.
